claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs lines 29-38: `var order = await repository.FindAsync(orderId) ?? throw new KeyNotFoundException($"order {orderId} not found");` then `order.Status = "cancelled"; await repository.SaveChangesAsync(); notifier.Send(order.Id, "order cancelled"); return order;`. No read of order.Status, so the r2 addition (`paid` is cancelled too) follows directly. Block matches source.

OrderServiceTests.cs@stage-1 has exactly two cancel tests (lines 46, 58): NewOrder seeds Status="new" and asserts "cancelled"; UnknownOrder asserts KeyNotFoundException for id 999. Neither reads FakeNotifier.Sent; no test seeds "shipped". Lines 65-67 comment: "No test here cancels a `shipped` order. The suite is green". `dotnet test DonHang.Tests` at stage-1 (r1): Passed 5, Failed 0. Block matches tools/extract-code (only an em-dash encoding artifact in the pipe).

story-example.md@stage-1 line 5: "hủy đơn hàng chưa thanh toán của mình"; AC3: "Khi đơn ở trạng thái `paid`, `shipped` hoặc `cancelled`, nút \"Hủy đơn\" không hiện."; AC4: "trả về 403 và không thay đổi gì"; AC5: "lần thứ hai trả về 409"; DoD: "Có test tự động cho mọi tiêu chí chấp nhận ở trên."

OrderServiceTests.cs@stage-1 contains 5 tests: three PlaceOrderAsync, CancelOrderAsync_NewOrder_SetsStatusCancelled, CancelOrderAsync_UnknownOrder_Throws. None seeds paid/shipped/cancelled, none involves another customer (403) or a second cancel (409). It is the only service test file under DonHang.Tests (git ls-tree stage-1), so the r2 sentence "none of them has a service test" also holds; CancelOrderAsync(int) takes no customer id.

Review practice stated by the outline itself (track.yaml outline items 1-3, near-verbatim); no versioned official doc governs it and the lesson hedges item 3 ("may be passing"). Treated as the lesson's method, not a factual claim.

Ledger kind is `opinion`, but this is behavior; verified by source. FakeOrderRepository@stage-1: `public void Seed(Order order) => orders[order.Id] = order;` and `FindAsync(int id) => Task.FromResult(orders.GetValueOrDefault(id));` return the same object; `SaveChangesAsync() => Task.CompletedTask`. A service that leaves Status untouched returns the seeded object with Status "cancelled", so Assert.Equal("cancelled", order.Status) passes. Lesson wording ("passes even if the service never changes the status") matches.

OrderServiceTests.cs@stage-1: every one of the 5 tests constructs its own fakes: lines 14-15 and 26-27 (`new FakeOrderRepository()`, `new FakeNotifier()`), line 40 and 60 (`new OrderService(new FakeOrderRepository(), new FakeNotifier())`), lines 48 and 50. The class has no instance fields; `OneItem` is a static expression-bodied property returning a new OrderItem per access.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and it redefines a term against the official meaning. .NET docs: "Code coverage is a measurement of the amount of code that is run by unit tests - either lines, branches, or methods." (refs/dotnet-docs/docs/core/testing/unit-testing-code-coverage.md:13). The lesson glosses coverage as a share of behavior checked; here the two cancel tests run every line of CancelOrderAsync, so by the standard meaning coverage is full. "share" also invites the percentage reading depth_notes excludes.
issues.quote: so it says nothing about coverage, the share of the new behavior that tests check
issues.fix: Replace with: "so it says nothing about whether each new behavior has a test that checks it; only matching tests to the new behavior does." If the word must be glossed, write "test coverage here means: each new behavior has a test that checks it" and add that to claims (kind definition, section 6). Do not use "share" or any number.

issues.text: "build" now means two things. Section 2 separates it from tests ("The build succeeds and every test passes"), so there it means compiling. Sections 4, 5 and summary 5 then say the build will show or catch a behavior break, which only a failing test does; compiling never catches it.
issues.quote: A missing test means the next change can break that behavior and the build will not show it.
issues.fix: Say "no test will fail" in section 4, "something a test catches" at the end of section 5, and "can be caught by a failing test, not by a bug report" in summary line 5. Keep "build" only for compiling, as in section 2.

issues.text: Claim 6 is filed as kind `opinion` with needs_verification false, but it states what a test does when run (a behavior claim), and it was verified against FakeOrderRepository. `opinion` would let it bypass evidence in later reviews.
issues.fix: In .meta.json claim 6 set "kind": "behavior" and "needs_verification": true; keep source_hint DonHang.Tests/FakeOrderRepository.cs@stage-1.
